visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A middle-aged male presenter with glasses and a black button-down shirt stands against a blurred green leafy background. He gestures expressively with his hands while speaking directly to the camera. (2) The scene cuts to a medium shot of a grey wolf lying on a rocky, shingle beach under overcast light. (3) Back to the presenter, who now holds a small black remote control, pointing it as if navigating a presentation. (4) A digital map of Southeast Alaska is overlaid, showing coastal islands and inland areas with colored markers indicating wolf pack distributions. (5) The video displays a scientific scatter plot graph with axes for Nitrogen-15 and Carbon-13 isotopes, showing distinct clusters for different wolf packs. (6) A bar chart appears, comparing total mercury (THg) concentrations in the livers of different Alaskan wolf populations. (7) A split-screen image shows a live wolf on the left and a decomposed wolf carcass inside a den on the right, labeled with 'A' and 'B'. (8) The presenter returns to the full frame, continuing his energetic explanation with rapid hand movements and varied facial expressions.
visual_base.text_narrative_log: (1) [Logo]: PanSci. [Slogan]: 一滴藥水逆轉老花? 挺健康揭真相. [Variety]: 抓到了! 牠下海偷吃. [Subtitle]: 我的天啊 牠竟然真的偷吃. (2) [Subtitle]: 而且還下海了. (3) [Subtitle]: 我們印象中灰狼在陸上打獵. (4) [Subtitle]: 但在阿拉斯加東南部. (5) [Subtitle]: 由阿拉斯加魚類及獵物部(ADF&G)的科學家. (6) [Subtitle]: Gretchen H. Roffler 帶領的團隊發現. (7) [Subtitle]: 狼群的菜單變了. (8) [Subtitle]: 而且有證據. (9) [Subtitle]: 因為其中一群狼體內「汞含量」. (10) [Subtitle]: 創下全球灰狼史上最高紀錄. (11) [Subtitle]: 不是特別值得高興的紀錄就是了. (12) [Subtitle]: 大約十年前 有科學家首次目擊. (13) [Subtitle]: 阿拉斯加的灰狼叼著海獺. (14) [Subtitle]: 但到底是這群「海景第一排」的狼. (15) [Subtitle]: 偶爾換換口味. (16) [Subtitle]: 剛好遇到飄來的熟成海獺肉. (17) [Subtitle]: 還是主動出擊 孩子愛吃已回購呢. (18) [Subtitle]: 這篇發表在《整體環境科學》(Science of the Total Environment). (19) [Subtitle]: 期刊上的研究 比較了三群狼. (20) [Subtitle]: 一群住在「普萊森特島 (Pleasant Island)」. (21) [Subtitle]: 其實就是快樂島上的島狼. (22) [Subtitle]: 一群是隔壁大陸的「古斯塔武斯 (Gustavus)」陸狼. (23) [Subtitle]: 而第三群是住在更內陸. (24) [Subtitle]: 完全不靠海的內陸狼 作為「對照組」. (25) [Subtitle]: 但科學家怎麼知道狼吞了什麼. (26) [Subtitle]: 看糞還是尿 都不是 是看毛. (27) [Subtitle]: 你都想看 蛤. (28) [Subtitle]: 研究分析了狼毛的「穩定同位素」. (29) [Subtitle]: 因為「你 就是你吃下去的東西」. (30) [Subtitle]: 首先看「碳-13」. (31) [Subtitle]: 陸地植物利用的碳-13比例很低. (32) [Subtitle]: 而海洋生物天生碳-13的比例高. (33) [Subtitle]: 所以一驗狼毛 發現碳-13數值飆高. (34) [Subtitle]: 就代表這傢伙吃了海產. (35) [Subtitle]: 再來生物在代謝的時候. (36) [Subtitle]: 會把輕的氮-14排掉 把重的氮-15留下. (37) [Subtitle]: 因此會在食物鏈裡一層層疊上去. (38) [Subtitle]: 所以從氮-15可以排出江湖地位. (39) [Subtitle]: 海獺是海洋的頂級掠食者. (40) [Subtitle]: 氮-15本來就很高. (41) [Subtitle]: 所以當一隻也很高的狼跑去吃海獺時. (42) [Subtitle]: 牠的氮-15當然又跳了一階. (43) [Subtitle]: 科學家再用穩定同位素混合模型. (44) [Subtitle]: 根據鹿、海獺、狼各自的同位素特徵 加以反推. (45) [Subtitle]: 結果不得了 快樂島上的狼 從2017年開始突然愛上海獺. (46) [Subtitle]: 呃 應該說 愛吃海獺. (47) [Subtitle]: 到現在飲食裡 68.7% 通通都是海獺. (48) [Subtitle]: 妙的是 甚至連比較近的大陸狼也學著吃. (49) [Subtitle]: 到2022年 大陸狼的主菜也變成了海獺 佔了50.1%. (50) [Subtitle]: 再次強調 海獺可是海洋食物鏈的上層. (51) [Subtitle]: 越上層經由「生物放大」. (52) [Subtitle]: 體內的甲基汞 (MeHg) 就越高. (53) [Subtitle]: 因此改吃海獺 Buffet 的狼. (54) [Subtitle]: 肝臟中的總汞濃度 (THg). (55) [Subtitle]: 是正常吃陸地動物的對照組「內陸狼」的 278 倍. (56) [Subtitle]: 這汞濃度不只是牠們小圈子裡第一. (57) [Subtitle]: 跟全世界所有文獻紀錄中的灰狼比 還是遙遙領先、刷新紀錄. (58) [Subtitle]: 即使中毒最輕的狼 都比其他國家的狼平均高 11 倍. (59) [Subtitle]: 最重的高出了 2000 倍. (60) [Subtitle]: 其中一隻 6 週前被抓捕過 代號 202006 的母狼. (61) [Subtitle]: 再次被發現時 已經是具屍體. (62) [Subtitle]: 肝臟的汞濃度是高到不可思議的 每克 64.3 微克. (63) [Subtitle]: 爆瘦 9 公斤 死於營養不良. (64) [Subtitle]: 難怪強如緋爾都寧願給人包養. (65) [Subtitle]: 科學家加碼驗了「硒」(Selenium). (66) [Subtitle]: 硒可以跟汞合體 變成無害的「硒化汞」 (HgSe) 來排毒. (67) [Subtitle]: 所有活著的狼體內的「硒汞摩爾比」 (Se:Hg) 都大於 1. (68) [Subtitle]: 代表牠們解毒劑夠 hold 得住. (69) [Subtitle]: 而死掉的 202006 只有 0.83. (70) [Subtitle]: 解毒系統被海獺灌到崩潰 太 Heavy Metal 了. (71) [Subtitle]: 好 所以狼吃了海獺 中毒了 連解毒機制也爆了. (72) [Subtitle]: 但回到最源頭 狼是怎麼在海裡找到海獺的. (73) [Subtitle]: 牠們是游泳、潛水 還是等海獺上岸再偷襲. (74) [Subtitle]: 是組隊還是單挑. (75) [Subtitle]: 已經有科學家架了多台野外攝影機. (76) [Subtitle]: 希望能直擊狼王子「下海偷吃」畫面 就讓我們繼續看下去.

The speaker exhibits professional broadcast clarity with frequent pitch modulation for emphasis. Underneath, a rhythmic electronic pop BGM provides a consistent upbeat energy. (2) A sharp digital 'ding' SFX coincides with the introduction of scientific data, where the speaker increases intensity to explain the mercury concentration findings. The acoustic environment is a clean studio recording with zero ambient interference. (3) The narrator's speech rate remains high and dense, maintaining high arousal as he describes the biological impact of sea otter consumption on wolves. The BGM remains steady with synthesized percussion. (4) A transition SFX occurs as the topic shifts to the specific case of a deceased wolf; the narrator's tone slightly lowers in pitch but retains a professional narrative drive. (5) The final phase features a concluding tone with a slight rise in pitch variability as the narrator poses rhetorical questions about wolf behavior, while the electronic beat continues until the sudden cutoff.

narrative_and_purpose.narrativeStructure: List-based: Hook -> Evidence Presentation -> Case Study -> Scientific Explanation -> Future Outlook
narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: To educate viewers on a recent scientific study regarding the shift in the diet of Alaskan wolves from land prey to sea otters, highlighting the resulting high mercury levels in their bodies and the biological magnification effect.
